title: Tor-independence for monoid-ideal quotients in a log regular chart
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ be its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$. Suppose a chart $c:P\to M|_W$ is given on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], and its induced map $P\to\overline M_{\bar w}=\overline M_{\bar x}$ is the chosen identification. Let $a:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be the composite of this chart with the structural map and the map to the geometric stalk. A monoid ideal means a subset $I\subseteq P$ with $I+P\subseteq I$, allowing $I=\varnothing$. For every monoid ideal $I$, writing $R=\mathbf Z[P]$, $IR$ for the ideal of $R$ generated by the monomials from $I$, and letting $R\to A$ be induced by $a$, one has$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_1(R/IR,A)=0.$$Here Tor is the module Tor functor of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, invoking Kato (1994), 6.1(ii), for Tor-independence of monoid-ideal quotients with the structure ring.

proof.text: By the sharp-chart statement $P$ is a finitely generated integral saturated sharp monoid, and the given chart $c$ is a chart of the kind used there, inducing the chosen identification $P\cong\overline M_{\bar x}$. Apply the completed-chart statement to it. It may replace $c$ by a chart $c':P\to M|_{W'}$ on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood, again inducing the chosen identification, and gives $n\ge0$ and an isomorphism, compatible with $a'(q)\mapsto z^q$ where $a'$ is the composite of $c'$ with the structure map, of $\widehat A$ with $B_k(P,n)$ (equal characteristic) or with $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$, $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ (mixed characteristic). We compare $a'$ with $a$. Since $P$ is sharp and $P\to\overline M_{\bar x}=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ is bijective, $a(q)$ is a unit only for $q=0$; so in the definition of a chart [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] the pushout is $P\oplus_{\{0\}}A^\times=P\times A^\times$, and $c$ gives a monoid isomorphism $P\times A^\times\cong M_{\bar x}$ with $c(q)\leftrightarrow(q,1)$ and $\alpha(q,v)=v\,a(q)$. The image of $c'(q)$ in $\overline M_{\bar x}$ is the image of $q$, so $c'(q)\leftrightarrow(q,u(q))$ with $u(q)\in A^\times$; since $c'$ is a monoid homomorphism and the monoid law on $P\times A^\times$ is componentwise, $u:P\to A^\times$ is a homomorphism, and $a'(q)=u(q)a(q)$ for all $q\in P$. Write $A_a$, $A_{a'}$ for $A$ with the $R$-algebra structures induced by $a$ and $a'$. Steps 2--5 prove $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_{a'})=0$, and Step 6 transfers this to $A_a$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (chart modelled on P at the geometric point and the two completed presentations); the comparison of two charts with the same characteristic identification is written out here

proof.text: Choose a Noetherian affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D$ containing the image $x$ of $\bar x$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}=D_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The affine strict-local comparison [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] gives a local isomorphism of $D$-algebras from $A$ to an algebraic strict henselization $D_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to the separable closure $K$ of $\kappa(x)$ in the field of $\bar x$; its index pairs $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ are the triples $(S,\ker\chi,\kappa(\ker\chi)\to K)$ over the closed point with the same morphisms, so it is the strict henselization of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. The isomorphism carries the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal, hence identifies the maximal-ideal completions, and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-completion-noetherian] gives that $\widehat A$ is Noetherian and $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat. Apply the coefficient base-change theorem [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] to $R\to A_{a'}\to\widehat A$ with $M=R/IR$ and $n=1$: it identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_{a'})\otimes_A\widehat A$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,\widehat A)$, where $\widehat A$ is an $R$-algebra through $a'$, i.e. through $z^q\mapsto z^q$ under the isomorphism of Step 1.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.4.3 proof, p. 110: passage from the strict local ring to its completed local chart; the flat Tor base-change step is written out here

proof.text: Equal characteristic. Put $S=k[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $B=B_k(P,n)$, the completion of $S$ at $(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Since $P$ is finitely generated, $S$ is a $k$-algebra of finite type, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $S\to B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]; $S$ is free over $k[P]$ on the monomials $t^e$, so $k[P]\to B$ is flat. Write $k[I]$ for the $k$-span of the $z^q$, $q\in I$; it is an ideal because $I+P\subseteq I$. The sequence $0\to k[I]\to k[P]\to k[P]/k[I]\to0$ is exact (the two outer terms are the spans of complementary subsets of the monomial basis), so tensoring with $B$ shows that $k[I]\otimes_{k[P]}B\to B$ is injective. As $R\to B$ factors through $k[P]=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}k$ and $IR=\bigoplus_{q\in I}\mathbf Zz^q$, one has $IR\otimes_RB\cong(IR\otimes_Rk[P])\otimes_{k[P]}B\cong k[I]\otimes_{k[P]}B$, compatibly with the multiplication maps. The Tor long exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] of $0\to IR\to R\to R/IR\to0$, with $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R,B)=0$, gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,B)=\ker(IR\otimes_RB\to B)=0$.

source.place: Agent proof from the monomial chart of Expose VI 1.6(i) and the Tor sequence used in Expose VIII 3.4.3

proof.text: Mixed characteristic. Put $S=C[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] as $C$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]; $\mathfrak a=(p,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_i)S$, $J_S=(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_i)S$; $B_0=B_C(P,n)$ the $\mathfrak a$-adic completion, $J=J_SB_0$, $B=B_0/(\theta)$. As in Step 3, $S\to B_0$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], so with $C[I]=\bigoplus_{q\in I}Cz^q$ we get an exact sequence $0\to C[I]\otimes_{C[P]}B_0\to B_0\to N\to0$, $N=B_0/IB_0$. (a) $\theta$ is injective on $N$. For $m\ge0$ the ideal $IS+J_S^{m+1}$ is the $C$-span of the monomials $z^qt^e$ with $q\in I$ or $q$ a sum of at least $m+1-|e|$ nonzero elements; as $P$ is sharp and generated by finitely many nonzero elements, only finitely many monomials lie outside it, so $Q_m=S/(IS+J_S^{m+1})$ is a free $C$-module of finite rank. Completion is exact on finite $S$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]; applied to $0\to IS+J_S^{m+1}\to S\to Q_m\to0$ and to a surjection $S^s$ onto the finitely generated ideal, it gives $N/J^{m+1}N=B_0/(IB_0+J^{m+1})\cong\widehat{Q_m}$; on $Q_m$ the $\mathfrak a$-adic and $p$-adic filtrations agree ($J_S^{m+1}Q_m=0$), and $Q_m$, free of finite rank over the $p$-adically complete $C$, is its own completion. So $N/J^{m+1}N\cong Q_m$ has no $p$-torsion. $B_0$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and $\mathfrak aB_0$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal](1), so $1+\mathfrak aB_0\subseteq B_0^\times$ by the geometric series and $J\subseteq\mathfrak aB_0$ lies in the Jacobson radical; hence $\bigcap_mJ^mN=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson]. If $x\in N$ is nonzero with $\theta x=0$, choose $m$ with $x\in J^mN\setminus J^{m+1}N$. Writing $\theta=p+j$ with $j\in J$ (completed-chart statement), $jx\in J^{m+1}N$, so $px\in J^{m+1}N$: the class of $x$ is a nonzero $p$-torsion element of $N/J^{m+1}N\cong Q_m$, a contradiction. (b) The snake lemma for multiplication by $\theta$ on the exact sequence above, with $\ker(\theta|N)=0$, makes $(C[I]\otimes_{C[P]}B_0)/\theta\to B_0/\theta B_0=B$ injective, i.e. $C[I]\otimes_{C[P]}B\to B$ is injective. As in Step 3, $IR\otimes_RB\cong C[I]\otimes_{C[P]}B$ compatibly with multiplication, and the Tor long exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,B)=0$. Small cases: $I=\varnothing$ ($N=B_0$) and $I=P$ ($N=0$) are included.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 give $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,\widehat A)=0$ for the $R$-structure through $a'$. By Step 2 this module is $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_{a'})\otimes_A\widehat A$, and $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat, so the consequence clause of [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_{a'})=0$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.4.3, p. 110, Tor-independence for the chosen chart

proof.text: Transfer to the given chart. By the Tor long exact sequence of $0\to IR\to R\to R/IR\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_b)=\ker(\mu_b:IR\otimes_RA_b\to A_b)$ for $b=a,a'$. As $IR=\bigoplus_{q\in I}\mathbf Zz^q$ and $R$ is spanned by the $z^r$, the module $IR\otimes_RA_b$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is $IR\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A$ modulo the elements $z^{q+r}\otimes x-z^q\otimes b(r)x$ ($q\in I$, $r\in P$, $x\in A$). The additive map $z^q\otimes x\mapsto z^q\otimes u(q)^{-1}x$ carries the relation for $a$ to that for $a'$: $z^q\otimes u(q)^{-1}a(r)x=z^q\otimes a'(r)u(q+r)^{-1}x\equiv z^{q+r}\otimes u(q+r)^{-1}x$, using $u(q+r)=u(q)u(r)$. It therefore induces $\psi:IR\otimes_RA_a\to IR\otimes_RA_{a'}$, with inverse given by $u(q)$ in place of $u(q)^{-1}$, and $\mu_{a'}\psi(z^q\otimes x)=a'(q)u(q)^{-1}x=a(q)x=\mu_a(z^q\otimes x)$. Hence $\psi$ maps $\ker\mu_a$ isomorphically onto $\ker\mu_{a'}=0$ (Step 5), and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A)=0$ for the structure of the statement, for every monoid ideal $I$; for $I=\varnothing$ the source $IR\otimes_RA$ is $0$, and for $I=P$ the quotient $R/IR$ is $0$.

lean.statement: theorem torOne_monoidIdeal_independence {X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}} (hlog : X.IsLogRegular) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) {W : X.scheme.Etale} (w : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t).fiber.obj W) {P : Type u} [CommMonoid P] (hP : IsFineSaturatedMonoid P) (c : P →* X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op W)) (hc : X.logStructure.IsChart W c) (e : P ≃* (X.logStructure.characteristic t)) (he : ∀ p : P, e p = Associates.mk (X.logStructure.toEtalePrelogStructure.germ t W w (c p))) (a : P →* strictLocalRing X.scheme t) (ha : ∀ p : P, a p = X.logStructure.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalkAlpha t (X.logStructure.toEtalePrelogStructure.germ t W w (c p))) (I : Set P) (hI : ∀ q ∈ I, ∀ p : P, q * p ∈ I) : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (MonoidAlgebra ℤ P)) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ P) (MonoidAlgebra ℤ P ⧸ Ideal.span {x : MonoidAlgebra ℤ P | ∃ q ∈ I, x = MonoidAlgebra.single q 1}))).obj (@ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ P) _ (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) inferInstance (Module.compHom (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) (MonoidAlgebra.lift ℤ (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) P a).toRingHom)))
